- Ele é fiel aos 4 primeiro filmes da franquia.

Agora, vamos aos pontos negativos (pelo menos pra mim).

- A dublagem em PTBR não é boa em algumas ocasiões, mas não chega a estragar o jogo.

[h1][b] Reseña de LEGO® Jurassic World[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
LEGO® Jurassic World es lo que pasa cuando mezclas Acción y Aventura con dinosaurios, humor de plastiquito y esa necesidad humana de romper todo para que salgan moneditas. Recorres momentos clave de las películas con el filtro LEGO: menos trauma, más slapstick, y cero responsabilidad por el caos que provocas (porque, claro, “se vuelve a armar”).

La propuesta es simple y efectiva: explorar, resolver rompecabezas ligeros, cambiar de personajes con habilidades específicas y abrirte paso a golpes (literalmente) por escenarios que coquetean con lo “mundo abierto” sin comprometerse del todo. La primera impresión es: “esto es para toda la familia”… hasta que te das cuenta de que vas a discutir con tu compañero de coop por quién se lleva los studs como si fueran herencia.

Si lo juegas en pantalla dividida o con Remote Play Together, se convierte en un experimento social: ¿cooperación? Sí. ¿Paz? No. Pero diversión, la hay.

[h2]Lo que Construyes vs. Lo que se Te Rompe[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
  Dinosaurios + LEGO = caos adorable y comedia visual que funciona sin esforzarse  
  Rompecabezas accesibles: perfecto para relajarte sin sentir que estás rindiendo un examen  
  Compatibilidad total con mando y pantalla dividida: coop local como debe existir en 2026  
  Steam Cloud + Remote Play (móvil/tableta/TV) + Remote Play Together: jugar donde sea y con quien sea, aunque sea para pelear por piezas  
  49 logros: suficiente zanahoria para completionists con paciencia de paleontólogo  

Lo No Tan Bueno:
  Dificultad generalmente baja: la IA y el reto están pensados para “no frustrar”, y a veces eso significa “no retar”   
  Fórmula LEGO muy marcada: rompes, construyes, cambias personaje, repites… y sí, lo volverás a hacer   
  Pantalla dividida puede sentirse caótica: dos jugadores, mucho en pantalla, y tu atención hecha migajas   
  “Mundo abierto” con comillas: exploras, sí, pero con estructura clara y zonas que se sienten más parque temático que libertad real

[h2]Conclusión (Bueno)[/h2]
LEGO® Jurassic World es un juego “bien hecho” en el sentido más literal: sabe lo que es, no pretende ser más, y te entrega Acción/Aventura ligera con rompecabezas y exploración amable. Si buscas desafío serio, aquí no hay: esto es para apagar el cerebro y encender el modo “romper cosas y rearmarlas”.

Lo controversial: funciona mejor como experiencia social (coop local/Remote Play Together) que como aventura “épica” en solitario. Solo, es simpático; acompañado, es una comedia involuntaria sobre la avaricia humana por moneditas LEGO.

Con 101 jugadores activos, no es el fenómeno del momento, pero 7144 recomendaciones totales dicen lo obvio: es un clásico de catálogo que mucha gente jugó, disfrutó y dejó en paz. Y eso está perfecto.

LEGO Jurassic World is one of the most charming and genuinely fun LEGO games ever made. It takes the already amazing Jurassic Park/Jurassic World universe and turns it into something hilarious, lighthearted, and surprisingly in-depth while still keeping all the excitement and adventure intact.

The humor in this game is fantastic. The cutscenes constantly had me laughing with the classic LEGO-style comedy, and somehow the game manages to parody iconic moments from the movies while also paying respect to them. It’s goofy in the best possible way.

What really surprised me though was how much content and detail the game has. There are so many dinosaurs to unlock, secrets to find, characters to play as, and areas to explore. The parks feel alive, and exploring places like Isla Nublar and Isla Sorna in LEGO form is honestly awesome.

The game is also incredibly relaxing to play. Whether you’re smashing objects for studs, solving puzzles, or just running around as a dinosaur causing chaos, it’s consistently entertaining. And despite the cartoony style, there’s still a lot of love and attention put into recreating scenes from all four original Jurassic films.

Visually, the game still looks great, the soundtrack is nostalgic, and the co-op gameplay makes it even better with friends or family. It’s one of those games that’s easy to pick up but hard to stop playing once you start collecting everything. And being able to make custom dinosaurs is freaking awesome!

If you love dinosaurs, LEGO games, or just want something funny and enjoyable to play, LEGO Jurassic World is absolutely worth it. It perfectly captures the fun side of the Jurassic franchise while still delivering a surprisingly deep and content-packed experience. TT Games never misses! I highly recommend LEGO Jurassic World!

LEGO Jurassic World Review
7/10
LEGO Jurassic World is a fun and simple game to 100% compared to most modern completionist games. The best adaptations are easily Jurassic Park and Jurassic World because it feels like the developers cared more about recreating those films.
The game’s biggest strength is the atmosphere and the ability to freely play as dinosaurs, especially custom dinosaurs like customised velociraptors.
However, the game becomes too samey over time. Most characters feel mechanically identical, and many dinosaurs don’t feel unique enough gameplay-wise. Some dinosaurs also feel underused, especially creatures like the Mosasaurus and Pterodactyl being restricted to small sections instead of being fully integrated into the open world.
Some collectibles were also more annoying than they should have been because of graphical bugs affecting certain roar triggers.
The game is also limited by the time period it released in, only covering the Jurassic films available at the time.

I really wanted to like the game, as there are funny moments and such buuut the gameplay* isn't that funny. I find it hard to come back to (like "I finished two other ~30h games in the meantime" hard), and I'll probably just watch the cutscenes somewhere instead of completing the game.

I assume it's funnier when you play it with someone else though; it shares the same gameplay with the Harry Potter collection, and it was easier to enjoy the game with a friend (I wished I had a dinosaur friend to play this game).

* The game depends on lot on the characters you have at hand : they all have specific perks to help you progress (but of course, you don't have all the perks first and need to come back later if you wish to unlock everything). The levels aren't really open (you are on rails with little exploration to unlock some small bonuses), but you can come back later with free play and different characters in order to complete it entirely.
What I don't really appreciate with this type of Lego games is the artificial replayability : you keep collecting coins and other stuff until you can unlock more characters / vehicles / dinosaurs and then you can come back to gather more coins and other stuff and proceeds to unlock more characters / vehicles / dinosaurs and then blablabla. It's not really appealing to me as it's increasingly repetitive and the actions don't vary that much.
